item.title: A heretical outrage: why Italians disown spaghetti bolognese
item.description: Spag bol carries my city’s name all over the world – to the embarrassment of restaurants in Bologna In Bologna, spaghetti bolognese does not exist. You’ll find it on menus in London and Sydney, in British school canteens and in jars on supermarket shelves across half the world, but not in the city that lent it its name. Order it in a trattoria beneath the Two Towers and at best you get a pitying smile. More often you’ll be brought a plate of tagliatelle, with a short lesson in local history on the side. Few of the Italian dishes famous abroad carry the name of a city. Every so often the argument flares up again over where pizza, carbonara or tiramisu were born. With spaghetti bolognese the parentage is written into the name, and yet, absurdly, it is the Bolognese themselves who disown it. Many regard it as an outrage, a heretical and misshapen version cooked only by people who know nothing of real Bolognese food. Continue reading...
